Effective Sample Sizes of Direct Proportions

Source: R/effective_trials.R
effective_trials.Rd

Effective sample sizes \(n_d / \mathrm{deff}_d\) for binomial area-level models (trials of hb_area and hb_twofold), from the direct proportions, their design variances and the sample sizes. The design effect of an area is undefined when its direct proportion is 0 or 1 (no design variance); such areas take a design effect pooled over their group, or a supplied fallback.

Usage

effective_trials(
  y,
  vardir,
  n,
  group = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  method = c("pooled", "area"),
  deff_fallback = NULL,
  deff_min = 1
)

Arguments

y

Vector, column name, or one-sided formula: direct proportions in \([0, 1]\).

vardir

Vector, column name, or one-sided formula: design variances of y.

n

Vector, column name, or one-sided formula: sample sizes (number of sampled units in the denominator of y).

group

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula: groups (e.g. provinces) within which design effects are pooled.

data

Optional data frame containing the variables.

method

"pooled" (default): every area takes the design effect of its group, \(\sum_d v_d / \sum_d \{y_d (1 - y_d) / n_d\}\) over the areas of the group with \(0 < y_d < 1\) (the ratio of the summed design variances to the summed simple random sampling variances). "area": each area takes its own design effect \(v_d / \{y_d (1 - y_d) / n_d\}\) where it is defined, and the pooled one otherwise.

deff_fallback

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula: design effects for the areas whose own design effect is undefined, used before the pooled ones with method = "area" (for instance the design effect of a related indicator of the same survey, which is defined where y is 0).

deff_min

Lower bound of the design effects (default 1, no gain over simple random sampling).

Value

A data frame with one row per area and columns n, deff (the design effect used, at least deff_min), deff_source ("area", "fallback", "group" or "overall") and trials (\(n_d / \mathrm{deff}_d\)). Areas with missing y or n get NA.

Details

Single-area design effects are noisy and undefined at \(y_d \in \{0, 1\}\), which is common for rare indicators. In a simulation of a two-stage cluster sample (12 provinces x 6 districts), effective sample sizes with design effects pooled per province gave 95% interval coverage of 0.925 (districts) and 0.937 (provinces), close to 0.929 and 0.946 with the true design effects, against 0.911 and 0.897 when the design was ignored (benchmarks/validation/binomial_neff.R in the source repository). A group without any area with \(0 < y_d < 1\) takes the design effect pooled over all areas.

References

  1. Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. John Wiley & Sons.

  2. Chen, C., Wakefield, J., and Lumley, T. (2014). The use of sampling weights in Bayesian hierarchical models for small area estimation. Spatial and Spatio-temporal Epidemiology, 11, 33–43.

See also

hb_area (family = "binomial"), gvf_smooth.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  prov = rep(1:3, each = 5), n = rpois(15, 80),
  y = c(0, rbeta(14, 2, 30))
)
d$vardir <- 1.6 * d$y * (1 - d$y) / d$n
effective_trials(~y, vardir = ~vardir, n = ~n, group = ~prov, data = d)
#>     n deff deff_source trials
#> 1  74  1.6       group 46.250
#> 2  91  1.6       group 56.875
#> 3  91  1.6       group 56.875
#> 4  83  1.6       group 51.875
#> 5  66  1.6       group 41.250
#> 6  84  1.6       group 52.500
#> 7  86  1.6       group 53.750
#> 8  85  1.6       group 53.125
#> 9  77  1.6       group 48.125
#> 10 72  1.6       group 45.000
#> 11 74  1.6       group 46.250
#> 12 77  1.6       group 48.125
#> 13 79  1.6       group 49.375
#> 14 79  1.6       group 49.375
#> 15 88  1.6       group 55.000

# own design effects where defined, pooled ones for y = 0
effective_trials("y", "vardir", "n", group = "prov", data = d, method = "area")
#>     n deff deff_source trials
#> 1  74  1.6       group 46.250
#> 2  91  1.6        area 56.875
#> 3  91  1.6        area 56.875
#> 4  83  1.6        area 51.875
#> 5  66  1.6        area 41.250
#> 6  84  1.6        area 52.500
#> 7  86  1.6        area 53.750
#> 8  85  1.6        area 53.125
#> 9  77  1.6        area 48.125
#> 10 72  1.6        area 45.000
#> 11 74  1.6        area 46.250
#> 12 77  1.6        area 48.125
#> 13 79  1.6        area 49.375
#> 14 79  1.6        area 49.375
#> 15 88  1.6        area 55.000
